response:
The meeting minutes are complete and verified. Both deliverables are in place at `out/纪要.docx` and `out/summary.json`.

**Result: 3 decisions, 2 action items, 1 risk, 6 total** — every item traces back verbatim to a transcript line, and `summary.json` matches the docx exactly.

The minutes split the seven transcript lines as follows:

- **一、决议事项** (3): 改空运、费用从模具预算出 (厂长 13:06)；就议定下来、周五前出首批报告 (质检方主任 13:09)；修模期间 2 号产线临时转产老型号 (厂长 13:11)
- **二、待办事项** (2, 表格): 修模并 10 月 18 日前复检 (模具科马工 13:02)；按欧盟标准重新送检 (质检方主任 13:08)
- **三、风险与关注** (1): 钢料海运赶不上则试产整体延期的风险 (采购吕经理 13:04)

The 13:00 opening line was dropped — it parses fine but contains none of the eleven keywords, so per the skill's rules it enters no section.

**On the 负责人/期限 columns**, which the brief constrained hardest, both action items came out 「待定」 for owner. That is the rule working, not a gap: the deterministic patterns require an explicit 「我负责／我们负责」, 「由X负责」, 「负责人是X」 or 「@X」 in the sentence itself. The transcript says 「我们需要修模」 and 「我们需要按欧盟标准重新送检」 — the speaker is implicit, never stated as an owner, so naming 模具科马工 or 质检方主任 would have been a guess. Only one deadline was extractable: 「10月18日之前」 from the explicit date in the 13:02 line. The 13:08 line has no time expression at all, so its deadline is 「待定」 too — I did not carry 「周五前」 across from the neighboring 13:09 line, since those are separate utterances and borrowing across them would be fabrication.

Verification I ran on the artifacts: python-docx reopens the file; the three section titles are byte-exact and in order; decision and risk numbering runs 1..n unbroken; the todo table is 3 columns with the 事项/负责人/期限 header; every item (including the table's 事项 column) matches a source line with the correct time and speaker; each owner/deadline value is either 「待定」 or found verbatim in its own source line; no item appears in two sections. Re-running the script reproduces an identical `summary.json`.

One environment note: the skill's script needs `python-docx`, which was not installed and the system Python is PEP 668 externally-managed. Rather than forcing a package into your system interpreter, I installed it into a throwaway venv at `/tmp/mmvenv` and ran the script with that interpreter. The deliverables are ordinary files and carry no dependency on it. If you want to regenerate later, `python3 -m venv` plus `pip install python-docx` in a local venv is the clean route. I also left the transcript at `fixtures/新模具试产评审会.txt` as the script input — the docx metadata line records that filename as its source.
